title: TA9-14418
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: XXXXX XXXX XXXXXX is a citizen of Mexico, seeking refugee protection pursuant to subsections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).1 ALLEGATIONS
The claimant has made three different statements with respect to what occurred in Mexico that led to his flight from the country. What follows is a summary of these three statements.

On XXXX, 2009 the claimant stated that he was a XXXX XXXX, Mexico City. One day he met a person XXXX who is associated with the criminal organization called the family. XXXX tried to get the claimant involved in his criminal activities. XXXX put his gun to the claimant's head on one occasion threatening to kill him or his family if he did not comply. The claimant states that many people went to his home with guns on one occasion at which time they beat him up and told him to listen to XXXX.

On XXXXX, 2009 the claimant stated that he fears for his safety from corrupt politicians of the PRI and PAN who are connected to the family drug cartel. He states that he has been threatened assaulted and persecuted because of his political affiliation and activities.

In an amended PIF narrative received at the IRB November 10, 2009 the claimant states that he was politically active with the PRD. He and his uncle used to organize political rallies. Their lives were threatened and the claimant fled to Mexico City to save his life. His uncle was assassinated on XXXXX, 2005. The assassins were looking for the claimant. The claimant was a gifted XXXXXXXX. In 2007 the claimant XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX. The claimant was always critical of PAN and PRI. On XXXXX, 2009 agents of the PGR disrupted a meeting and threatened the participants that if they didn't stop criticizing PRI and PAN they would be taken and tortured and killed. On XXXXX, 2009 members of the PRD party who were at that meeting begin receiving written death threats. The claimant began to receive death threats. On XXXXX, 2009 his wife kicked him out of the house because she wanted him to stop his political activities and he insisted because he wanted to dedicate his life to ending corruption in Mexico. On XXXXX, 2009 he and his friend were stopped by eight uniformed men from the PGR. They were beaten and tortured. They were told this was so they would leave the PRI and PAN politicians alone. They were told that they could be found anywhere in Mexico. The claimant was hospitalized for four days. On XXXXX, 2009 he moved to his aunt's home in Chihuahua state. He began to organize political activities of the local youth. During one of the meetings eight individuals in the AFI arrested him, took him to an unknown house and beat him. His aunt recommended he leave the country. He relocated to Michoacan state, and stayed with a friend of his aunt. On XXXXX, 2009 when he went to visit his wife in Mexico City she told him that the people who had killed his uncle in 2005 had come looking for him and that the police would not help. One of his neighbors told him that armed men had been asking for him. On XXXXX some members of the family came looking for the claimant but he and his brother were able to flee. The claimant went to the public Ministry who told him that they could not help against the family and advised that he should leave the country.

The day prior to the hearing and at the hearing itself the claimant requested a postponement so that he could have legal representation to present his claim. After carefully considering the adjournment request and the factors that the division must consider as outlined in rule 48 this request was denied. What was of particular relevance in rejecting this request was the fact that the claimant had been referred to the IRB in July 2009. The claimant made a statement in July 2009 that at that time he was in the process of retaining a lawyer. The claimant was present in assignment court on January 27, 2011 at which time the right to counsel was explained to him and this matter was set to proceed peremptorily. The claimant signed a confirmation of readiness to proceed on the hearing date. There were no exceptional circumstances. For these reasons his request for postponement was turned down. In response the claimant stated he would not answer any questions he was asked at the hearing. The panel advised him that nonetheless he would be asked some questions. The claimant maintained his silence until the third of fourth time he was asked what happened in Mexico and why he is afraid to return.

I find the claimant is not a Convention refugee pursuant to Section 96, as he does not have a well-founded fear of persecution in Mexico for any of the five Convention grounds. I further find the claimant is not a person in need of protection under Section 97 as, on a balance of probabilities, his removal to Mexico would not subject him personally to a risk to life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment or to a danger of torture. My analysis is as follows. ANALYSIS Identity
The claimant's identity as a national of Mexico was established by his Mexican passport a true copy of which is on file. Credibility

I find that the claimant did not provide sufficient credible and trustworthy evidence to support his fear of returning to Mexico. There were a large number of significant inconsistencies between statements the claimant gave at the hearing and allegations contained in the claimant's earlier written statements. These inconsistencies were not adequately explained. As a result of these concerns I do not accept, on a balance of probabilities, the claimant's allegations with respect to what occurred in Mexico that led to his flight.

In these reasons I shall focus on what I consider to be the most significant inconsistencies and omissions. A non-exhaustive list of the inconsistencies that led me to the above conclusion are as follows:

During the hearing the claimant stated that on one occasion men had gone to a PRD meeting uttering threats. He initially stated that he had no idea of the identity of these people. He then stated that they were wearing uniforms and that he does not recall what kinds of uniforms they were wearing. This incident appears to be detailed in the claimant's statement received November 10, 2009 (from now on referred to as the PIF narrative). In this description the men are clearly described as agents of the Federal Attorney General's office. The claimant was asked to explain why he stated during the hearing that he did not know who these men were and did not know what uniform they were wearing. The claimant's explanation is that he does not remember. This explanation fails to address the concern. I find this evidence undermines the claimant's credibility.

The claimant described an incident which occurred on XXXXX, 2009 when he and his friend were stopped by state agents. During the hearing the claimant stated that he was driving from his friend's house to the house of a PRD member. The PIF narrative statement indicates that they were driving to his friend's house. The claimant was asked to explain the discrepancy. He stated that he was confused and mixed up. I am not persuaded by this explanation as it fails to address the inconsistency. I think it is reasonable to expect the claimant to provide a consistent statement as to whether he and his friend were assaulted as they were driving to his friend's house or from his friend's house. I find this evidence undermines the claimant's credibility.

The claimant alleges that because of problems he was having in Mexico City he relocated to his aunt's home. During the hearing he was asked to describe what led to his decision to leave his aunt's home. He stated that he received a threat. He was asked to describe the circumstances in which he received the threat and stated that he could not recall. I think it is reasonable to expect the claimant to be able to recall the circumstances of the threat that led to his decision to leave his aunt's home in XXXX 2009. His inability to do so further undermines his credibility. More significantly the claimant failed to make any reference to the circumstances that led to his decision to leave his aunt's home as described in the PIF narrative. In that narrative the claimant states that he was kidnapped by unknown people, beaten and tortured and left unconscious on the side of a highway. As a consequence of this incident the claimant left his aunt's. The claimant was asked to explain why he omitted any reference to this incident at the hearing. He stated he did not understand the questions he was asked with respect to what happened that led to his departure from his aunt's. I am not persuaded by this explanation. He was clearly asked to describe what happened. He responded that he had received a threat however he could not recall the details of the threat. I find he did understand the question and I further find this evidence seriously undermines his credibility.

The claimant was asked to explain why in his initial statement provided on July 9, 2009 as to why he fled to Mexico he failed to make any reference to fear of any political parties in Mexico or of his own involvement in any political parties (as outlined above in the allegations section). The claimant's explanation was that he was afraid when he came to Canada. He further stated that he was afraid to refer to the Mafia as they may be present in Canada. I am not persuaded by this explanation. Firstly the fact that the claimant might have been in fear does not explain why he would fail to make any reference to the political nature of his problems in Mexico. Secondly the claimant's statement in question does in fact refer to "the family" which is the criminal organization or Mafia he is referring to. I find this evidence further undermines the claimant's credibility.

In his first statement the claimant stated that associates of XXXX went to his home with guns, beat him up, and told him that he should listen to XXXX. There is no reference to this incident in the latter two written statements. The claimant made no reference to this when he was asked during the hearing to describe his interactions and the situation with XXXX. The claimant was asked to explain. He stated that due to a lack of counsel he is having problems. He stated that legal aid denied his request for representation. I am not persuaded by this explanation. His lack of representation does not logically explain why he would make a statement of a significant incident when he initiated his refugee claim that appears to be inconsistent with or omitted from later statements. I find this evidence further undermines the claimant's credibility.

At the outset of the hearing the claimant stated that his PIF was not interpreted to him in Spanish. He stated that he does not understand any of the document as it is written in English. It was pointed out to the claimant that according to the PIF he and an interpreter signed a declaration on July 16, 2009 that the entire contents of this document had been interpreted in Spanish to the claimant. The name of the interpreter was mentioned to the claimant. He stated this person was never an interpreter. The claimant was asked if he knew the interpreter. The claimant indicated that this person had helped him with his refugee claim. The claimant stated he was unable to say how this person helped him because he could not remember. I find this evidence further undermines the claimant's credibility. The claimant signed a declaration as did an interpreter. Without anything compelling to suggest otherwise I take this declaration at face value to be an accurate statement. The claimant's statement that he was helped by the interpreter but that he cannot remember how he helped I find somewhat suspicious. I think it is reasonable to expect the claimant to be able to remember how this person assisted him with his refugee claim.

The claimant has provided a number of personal documents to corroborate some of his allegations. There is a document to corroborate that he was associated with the PRD. There is a letter from the claimant's cousin who indicates that a number of years ago the claimant and his cousin's father received death threats for denouncing corrupt politicians. There is a medical report indicating that on XXXXX, 2009 the claimant was hospitalized for four days after being attacked. These documents have been reviewed and considered. I find that they do not resolve the significant concerns I have with respect to the credibility of the claimant's specific allegations. In my assessment of the totality of the evidence before me and in particular consideration of the credibility concerns I have with respect to this claimant I am assigning these documents little weight.

As a consequence of the concerns outlined above I find that the claimant has failed to prove, on the balance of probabilities, the allegations of material fact on which his refugee claim is based. I do not accept on the balance of probabilities that he is currently being pursued by criminal or political elements in Mexico.

To summarize, I find the claimant's evidence lacking in credibility with respect to the events material to his refugee claim. Therefore, I find there is not a serious possibility of persecution should he return to Mexico. I therefore conclude that the claimant has failed to establish a well-founded fear of persecution under Section 96 of IRPA, and for these same reasons I find that the claimant is not a person in need of protection or at a risk to life, or risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, or a danger of torture as set out in Section 97 of IRPA and therefore his claim is denied. (signed) "K. Fainbloom" K.
